newsitem.title: UK: BP, British GAS reach gas accord.
newsitem.headline: BP, British GAS reach gas accord.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc and British Gas Plc said on Thursday that they had reached agreement over "take-or-pay' North Sea gas contracts under which British Gas was contracted to buy gas at uneconomic prices.

BP will receive compensating payments in return for giving British Gas relief on volumes of gas it must lift and on price. British Gas said it had agreed to pay total compensation of 293 million pounds ($484 million).

The "take-or-pay' contracts, which British Gas has with other suppliers as well as BP, have proved a potentially massive financial burden on the company. Since they were struck, British Gas' share of the British industrial market has shrunk rapidly, and the price of gas has fallen. In addition, the British household gas market is about to be opened up to competition.

British Gas Executive Director Roy Gardner said, "I am delighted that these important gas contracts have been re-negotiated...They will relieve some of our "take-or-pay' obligations and lead to reduced costs as we prepare for market liberalisation."

Rodney Chase, BP Exploration Chief Executive, said he believed it was an agreement with which both companies could be pleased, adding it "meets our objective of retaining value for BP's shareholders as well as creating extra flexibility for our gas marketing business."

British Gas said its own gas production arm had reached similar agreements on contracts it has with British Gas Trading. Separately, British Gas said it would seek approval from shareholders on February 12 1997 for its planned demerger into a gas sales and trading business -- to be called Centrica -- and the remaining British Gas business, comprising its Transco transportation system and its exploration and production unit. ($1=.6054 Pound)
